name: Jacob Hufty
bio: a Representative from New Jersey; likely born in Pennsylvania, ca. 1750; blacksmith by trade; served in the Revolutionary War as a private in the New Jersey state militia; freeholder for Salem Township, N.J., 1792; elected overseer of the poor and collector of Salem Township, N.J., 1793; county justice of Salem County, N.J., 1797, county judge in 1798, and county justice and judge, 1804; served as sheriff 1801-1804; freeholder of Salem Township, N.J., 1800-1804; a director of the board of chosen freeholders, 1801; member of the New Jersey state council, 1804, 1806, and 1807; county collector, 1805-1808; judge of Orphans Court, 1805-1808; surrogate in 1808; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Eleventh and Twelfth Congresses and as a Federalist to the Thirteenth Congress (March 4, 1809-May 20, 1814); died on May 20, 1814, in Salem, N.J.; interment in St. John's Episcopal Churchyard.
